title: RPZ repair: match the failed component to the exact assembly
description: RPZ repair begins with the exact model, size, failed check or relief finding, and installation condition.
prompt: Which RPZ condition is being repaired and what must happen afterward?
answer: RPZ repair begins with the exact model, size, failed check or relief finding, and installation condition. Relief discharge can be a diagnostic symptom; the correct repair path is not established by the discharge alone.
urgency: Escalate uncontrolled discharge, body damage, freeze damage, drainage hazards, or a system that cannot be safely isolated.
diagramAlt: Backflow service and compliance workflow reference
identifiers: Record relief-valve discharge separately from upstream or downstream leakage.
Match any kit or internal component to the exact RPZ model and nominal size.
A required test and report remain separate from mechanical repair work.

choices.label: I have a notice or program requirement
choices.detail: Use the issuing program to verify deadline and filing requirements.

choices.label: The assembly failed or needs service
choices.detail: Document the device and define repair plus retest scope.

choices.label: I manage a commercial asset
choices.detail: Separate access, shutdown, testing, and closeout responsibilities.

steps.title: Establish the exact record
steps.body: Document whether water is from the relief opening, cover, test cock, shutoff, or piping connection.

steps.title: Define the specific scope
steps.body: Use the nameplate and manufacturer record to identify the exact parts path and service limits.

steps.title: Prove the closeout
steps.body: Include isolation, drainage, repair, certified retest, and required filing in the written scope.

safeChecks: Keep the relief opening visible and unobstructed.
Photograph the full assembly before authorizing a kit.
Confirm drainage implications before a relief-related repair.
stopConditions: The body is cracked or distorted.
The relief discharge is uncontrolled or creates property damage.
notThisDevice: A generic service listing does not establish program eligibility.
A device family is not enough to identify compatible parts.
This page does not replace a qualified assessment or authority approval.
